title: Heel-of-the-knife mince: shallots and garlic with precise control
summary: Lan Lam demonstrates an alternative to traditional shallot mincing by using the heel of a non-bolster knife to make vertical cuts first, enabling tighter spacing and improved control since the distance between the back of the blade and the wrist is smaller. This method is contrasted with the conventional horizontal-then-vertical approach and is extended to garlic, where she shows skipping horizontal cuts and completing the mince with a 90-degree clove flip and a final pass. The video emphasizes knife anatomy (the bolster) and a gentle rocking motion to guide the blade straight down, yielding uniform pieces suitable for vinaigrettes and pan sauces. The tips focus on precision, blade alignment, and practice, with encouragement to try the technique on a couple of shallots before applying it in recipes.

sections.title: Traditional shallot mincing: setup and challenge
concepts: traditional mincing method (horizontal first, then vertical)
blade tip distance from wrist affects accuracy
knife anatomy: bolster absence reduces control
sections.description: Lan introduces the conventional approach to mincing shallots—start with horizontal cuts, then move to vertical ones—and explains why it’s tricky. The small size of shallots requires closely spaced cuts, and the distance from the blade tip to the wrist makes precise placement hard.

sections.title: Heel-of-knife vertical cuts for shallots
concepts: vertical cuts from the knife heel
sections.description: The technique shifts to using the heel of a non-bolster knife to perform vertical cuts, enabling closer spacing and steadier control. A gentle rocking motion guides the blade straight down, leveraging the shorter back-of-knife distance for precision.

sections.title: Garlic adaptation: no horizontal cuts, 90-degree flip
sections.description: The heel-of-the-knife method is extended to garlic: avoid horizontal cuts, make a single across move, then flip the clove 90 degrees to continue mincing.

sections.title: Final passes for garlic mince
sections.description: After the 90-degree flip, the mince is completed with the final passes to achieve a clean, uniform garlic mince.

sections.title: Results: precision, uniform pieces, and uses
sections.description: The technique yields precise, uniform pieces and is presented as ideal for vinaigrettes and pan sauces. The host emphasizes that practice helps develop the skill.

sections.title: Practice tips and closing
concepts: practice on a couple shallots first
sections.description: Closing encouragement to practice on a few shallots before applying the technique in recipes, with a nudge to explore more techniques at cooksillustrated.com.
